clue.text: The costs of accommodation in some apparent slums!

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wry remark that people pay good money to live in run-down housing.
explanation.definitionFit: Rents are the regular payments a tenant makes for a place to live.

clue.text: The fisherman's fish

definitions.meaning: a fisherman with rod and line; the possessive reads 'the fisherman is'
the anglerfish, a deep-sea fish that lures prey with a fleshy lure on its head

explanation.surface: A question of which fish the fisherman landed or favours.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a person who fishes with rod and line and the sea creature also called the anglerfish.

clue.text: The quintessential show business entertainer?

parts.note: read 'show business' literally: a performer whose act is to show her private parts, the 'business', in a strip show

explanation.surface: Asking who is the archetypal star of the entertainment world.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who undresses on stage literally shows everything, a cheeky reading of the showbiz phrase.

clue.text: If you're on it, you may get off

definitions.text: If you're on it, you may get off

parts.words: If you're on it, you may get off
parts.note: an airline passenger waiting for a spare seat may eventually get off the ground, or get off the list, by flying

explanation.surface: A riddle about a vehicle you board and might alight from.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller on the reserve list waiting for an unclaimed seat may yet get away on the flight.

clue.text: Firm that you might mean?

definitions.meaning: a firm is a company or commercial concern
the idiom 'mean ...' means to be serious about something, so this is what you might mean

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether 'firm' is really the word you intended.
explanation.definitionFit: A company is a commercial enterprise, and to be serious is to 'mean' it in the idiom about earnestness.

clue.text: Deny it nothing? Going back in to bargain

indicators.note: in says the turned letters are put inside the word for deny

parts.note: to deny something is to negate it

indicators.note: going back tells us to read the words it and nothing in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
zero, the round letter O

explanation.surface: Advice to a negotiator: refuse everything, then return to the table to haggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going back' turns the two pieces round to OTI, and 'in' places that inside the word for deny; 'Going back in' reads as returning to talks, hiding both signals.
explanation.definitionFit: To bargain is to haggle over terms, which is what parties do when they talk a deal through.

clue.text: The French queen goes round immediately to put it back

indicators.note: goes round says the queen's word encircles the other piece

parts.note: in French a queen is la reine
stat, from Latin statim, is medical shorthand for at once

explanation.surface: A French queen hurries round restoring something to its proper place.
explanation.walkthrough: STAT is medical slang for 'right now', used on hospital orders.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something or someone to a former position is to return it there.

clue.text: An artist tends to be ruder when disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed letters are jumbled out of place, so the word ruder is rearranged

explanation.surface: A painter grows rude when someone interrupts him at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Albrecht Dürer was the great German Renaissance painter and engraver.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a German painter and printmaker, so he is one example of the type.

clue.text: The left might label him a tragic figure

indicators.note: the clue says the L might be added to this man to make the word label, so removing it from label leaves him

parts.note: L is the usual abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Political opponents might brand him a tragic figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as L plus him might make LABEL: so take L from LABEL. 'The left' is not a political party here. Abel, son of Adam, was killed by his brother Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Abel is murdered by his brother Cain, making him the Bible's first victim of killing.

clue.text: A stable, one on stud property

parts.note: a stall is a single compartment for an animal in a stable
the Roman numeral I is one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advertising a stable that comes with one stud farm as part of the property.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncastrated male horse kept for breeding is the main asset of a stud farm.

clue.text: One here, in a seaside resort, having abandoned Ghana

indicators.note: having abandoned says the letters for Ghana are left out of the resort's name

parts.note: Brighton is a resort on England's south coast
GH is the international vehicle code for Ghana

explanation.surface: A visitor in a seaside town who has given up living in Ghana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here' means Britain, from the British newspaper's point of view. BRIGHTON is a seaside resort on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Britain is a native of this country, where the clue is published.

clue.text: Send back some gin

indicators.note: send back says the word for some is returned in reverse order

parts.note: some of a thing is part of it

explanation.surface: A drinker returning a measure of gin to the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' is not the drink but a snare for catching game.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare for catching animals, another name for a device that catches game.

clue.text: Report that city speculator dined at home?

indicators.note: the question mark warns that the phrase is only a loose match when spoken, a pun on the sound

parts.note: a bull is a stock-market speculator who buys expecting prices to rise; the City is London's financial district; to eat at home rather than out is to eat in

explanation.surface: A news item asking whether a City trader stayed in for supper.
explanation.walkthrough: BULL ATE IN, said quickly, sounds like the answer; the question mark signals the pun. The City is London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official news statement, a kind of report.

clue.text: Does rage sound ominous? It certainly could be

indicators.note: could be says the letters of rage sound may become another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether an angry noise is a threatening one, and agreeing that it might be.
explanation.definitionFit: Something threatening and likely to cause harm is foreboding, carrying a sense of risk.

clue.text: Subjects for discussion at dull royal society meeting

parts.note: a matt finish is dull, not shiny
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher

explanation.surface: Topics raised at a tedious gathering of the Royal Society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' and 'meeting' only join the pieces; ER is the Queen's monogram.
explanation.definitionFit: Matters are affairs or issues that people talk about.

clue.text: An element of hesitation one has initially, following such a legendary figure

indicators.note: following says the I and the hesitation come after the legendary figure

parts.note: a Titan is one of the giant gods of Greek myth

indicators.note: has initially says the one goes at the start, before the hesitation

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
um is the sound of a pause in speech

explanation.surface: A trace of doubt that a mythic hero first feels.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanium is a metallic chemical element, number 22 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Feeling of the upper house that society should be integrated

indicators.note: integrated means taken in and made part of the whole, so S goes inside

parts.note: the Senate is the upper chamber of a legislature such as the US Congress

explanation.surface: The upper chamber's view that society ought to be desegregated.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensate means perceiving through the senses, so able to sense physically.

clue.text: A member of the community

parts.note: the community is the ... Community, forerunner of the EU, so this is a citizen of one of its states

explanation.surface: A plain description of someone who belongs to a local group.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of a nation in the European Community belongs to that union of states.

clue.text: Progressed by coach or rail?

parts.note: a sportsman who improved under a coach was taught and drilled; a traveller by rail went by locomotive

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone travelled by bus or by rail.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone coached has been taught a skill, and someone who went by rail travelled by locomotive.

clue.text: In a large reptile, it could be a disruptive influence

indicators.note: In says the word it goes inside the reptile

parts.note: gator is short for alligator
taken as written

explanation.surface: Within a big crocodilian lurks a troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator stirs up unrest, a troublemaker who causes disruption.

clue.text: River 2 would happily try out

definitions.meaning: the ... in Hampshire, England, is a famous chalk-stream trout river, a place a fisherman would love
to try out is to trial or examine

explanation.surface: A fishing river the man of 2-down would gladly sample.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 refers to the answer of 2-down, the fisherman. The Test is a celebrated trout river in Hampshire, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names a Hampshire trout stream and means to trial something to see if it works.

clue.text: It's competitive, of course

definitions.meaning: a horse ... is run over a course, so the event belongs to a course

explanation.surface: A remark that something is naturally a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest of speed is competitive, and such contests are run on a racecourse.

clue.text: Given credit note, socks were settled on

parts.note: C is an abbreviation for credit
hose are stockings or socks

explanation.surface: Someone given a credit note decides to spend it on socks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chosen has been picked or decided on.

clue.text: County cricketer on-side?

parts.note: Kapil Dev was a famous Indian cricket all-rounder
in cricket the on side, also called the leg side, is abbreviated ON

explanation.surface: Asking whether a county cricketer bats on the leg side.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; the on side is the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Devon is an English county in the south-west of the country.

clue.text: Fashions for shirts with a split down the middle

indicators.note: down the middle says the split goes into the centre of the shirts

parts.note: TS is short for T-shirts
a rend is a split or tear

explanation.surface: Trendy shirts sporting a slash right down the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Trends are fashions, the styles currently in vogue.

clue.text: Doe limps badly, then collapses

indicators.note: badly says the letters of the words doe limps are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A deer hobbles along painfully and then falls over.
explanation.definitionFit: To implode is to fall in on itself, caving inward.

clue.text: Unearthed a Dutch dog to back

indicators.note: to back says the dog's name is read backwards

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: Digging up a Dutch dog to support it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unearthed has been excavated from the ground.

clue.text: Tales that made Rome dance with excitement?

indicators.note: excitement stirs things up, so the letters of Rome dance are mixed

explanation.surface: Stories so thrilling that the people of Rome danced.
explanation.walkthrough: Boccaccio's Decameron is a 14th-century collection of a hundred Italian stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Boccaccio's Decameron is a famous medieval collection of stories.
